timecoded_text_to_speech.text: In this experiment, we will study the reaction between lead nitrate and potassium iodide.
For this, we will need lead nitrate salt, potassium iodide salt, two test tubes, a test tube holder, spatula, water and a dropper.
Take about half a spatula full of lead nitrate salt in a test tube and fill it up to one fourth full with water.
Now shake the test tube till the salt is dissolved to prepare an aqueous solution of lead nitrate.
Similarly, prepare an aqueous solution of potassium iodide in a separate test tube.
Add the aqueous solution of potassium iodide to the aqueous solution of lead nitrate.
You will observe a yellow colored precipitate is immediately formed in the test tube.
A chemical reaction in which there is a mutual exchange of ions between the reacting compounds is called a double displacement reaction.
In this reaction, lead nitrate and potassium iodide react with each other to form lead iodide and potassium nitrate.
As there is a precipitate of lead iodide formed in this reaction, this is also an example of precipitation reaction.

About India Literacy Project:
India Literacy Project, ILP, is a volunteer based non-profit organization dedicated to the cause of literacy in India. By empowering every individual we serve with functional literacy and an understanding of their basic rights and responsibilities, we strive to be a catalyst for 100% literacy in India.

About MDLS:
ILP's Multi-Dimensional Learning Space (MDLS) is a program that provides learning opportunities to school children to explore, experiment, discover, and learn in multiple ways. The concept of Schools as multi-dimensional learning spaces is based on the foundation that 1) Equal importance should be given to all aspects of the curriculum 2) Learning is not restricted to a curriculum. It should extend to help holistic and balanced development of a child 3) One learning style doesn't work for all and 4) Learning should involve visual, auditory and experiential methods.

About MDLS Science Experiment Kit: 
The Science Experiment Kit is one of the key elements of ILP’s Multi-Dimensional Learning Space (MDLS) program. MDLS has been enabling students to learn Science through hands-on experiments, showing learning Science can be simple, fun, inexpensive and can be done with items you can easily find around you, without many specialized or expensive equipment. The Kit contains material required to do experiments covering around 200+ concepts from 5th to 10th Grade across Physics, Chemistry and Biology.
